title: Travelling in Nepal - Questions and Answers
body:
O.P.
Just making this thread because I couldn't find a recent one.
I'll be in nepal kathmandu for 1 month for a university placement (35 hours week) so outside that I'm planning to see kathmandu as much as possible and weekends go out into the regional areas (short treks – pokhora). We will skip going to chitwan.
At the moment in Thamel in a hotel but will be with my host family for the month from tomorrow.
What are some recommendation places/restaurants/lounges and any tips on nepal.

---- replies ----
[User #34420819712 postsbeedyWhirlpool Forums Addict] UltraBoost writes...
some recommendation places/restaurants/lounges and any tips on nepal.
Utse restaurant in Thamel for Tibetan and Nepalese food.
Part day trip to Monkey Temple for views over Kathmandu. Also worth at least a half day to Bhaktapur outside Kathmandu.
Assuming you have weekends off – Fly to Pokhara Sat morning, stay overnight, return Sunday afternoon. Be one of the first to board so you get views of the Himalayas enroute. Sit right side to Pokhara, left on return.
Things to do include boat ride on lake or ride across lake to World Peace Pagoda. Sarangkot Paragliding in Pokhara can pick you up from your hotel, take you to a mountain behind Pokhara, tandem paraglide to Pokhara and back to hotel. If you don't want to paraglide you can hire a car to take you to up to Sarangkot for nice views. Ultralight flights can be booked from Pokhara.
[User #30444497 postsflaggycreekForum Regular] Mainstream Katmandu restaurants – roadhouse, fire & ice, helenas. Cheap & good – try Ace cafe around corner from Z street, Gaia does nice breakfast. Coffee – Himalayan Java, pumpernickel. Try the tongba at Utse. Depends how active you are – I did a social mtb ride with Himalayan single track one morning and also a 2 day ride. Do day trips to Patan & Bhaktapur, consider hiring a local guide for a few dollars when you get there. Get good shoes and walk everywhere. Walk to Durbar square, swayambayu temple etc. Learn how to cook Nepalese with your host. Andrew

Hello guys,
any recommendations on what to do in Pokhora?
went paragliding today for the first time and it was amazing – at 10am. then got back to hotel and went with a guide (part of hotel package) to the fewa lake and took a boat to the world peace temple site and walked up. After that went to another cave and waterfall. Any idea on what to do tomorrow?
I'm thinking of more site seeing etc or anything interesting around fewa lake.
Thanks
[User #34420819712 postsbeedyWhirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
UltraBoost writes...
what to do tomorrow?
Ultralight if you can afford. Some companies have a 30 minute flight close to Fishtail Mountain that's a good option for a great experience that's not too costly imo. I don't regret spending up on the 1 ½ hour flight – it's a memory that will stay with me forever, one of the highlights of decades of travel. http://www.fishtailexperiences.com/index.php Try to go early as possible as that's often when you get the best conditions.
Edit: Great video showing what it's like on the 60 minute flight – https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E3tGJXAG8e8
[User #34420819712 postsbeedyWhirlpool Forums Addict] Bertt writes...
Any recommendations for upmarket hotels in Kathmandu, for 3-4 nights?
Yak and Yeti is a long established upmarket favourite that's close to attractions yet set back from the hustle and bustle. I'd also consider the Dalai-La Boutique Hotel.
Can't comment on other newer, more expensive places I haven't seen.
[User #97511739 postsLBDuckWhirlpool Enthusiast] Well this seems the most recent of the Nepal threads.
About to book an 8 day tour for my wife and I to Kathmandu, Chitwan NP, Nagarkot & Bhaktapur – it's a small tour. We're both early 60s so won't be climbing too many mountains! We're looking at going mid February. We're also adding on an additional 3 days for ourselves in Kathmandu at the end.
As this thread is quite old looking for recent thoughts, ideas what to do in our own 3 days in Kathmandu etc.
[User #34420819712 postsbeedyWhirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
LBDuck writes...
ideas what to do in our own 3 days in Kathmandu etc.
It depends on your interests and what you are after, and how much energy you have left after your tour. Also your budget. I would probably stay in Thamel, it's touristy but convenient. I liked the kathmandu Guest house, a great place to wind down at the end of a tour. https://youtu.be/edYW-F_CTgA?si=c-PdqXFT0k-y2QGp
Having been to all 3 places on your tour, I have to say Bhaktapur was my favourite, though it was in 1989, so things might have changed. I have been to Nepal a few times between 1971 and 2014 – my word, how it has changed.
Do you have to spend all 3 days in Kathmandu? If not, and time and budget allows, I suggest a return flight to Pokhara, leaving early one morning and returning that evening. Edit: For spectacular mountain views (subject to weather) sit on the right side of the plane outbound, and the left returning. While in Pokhara take a boat ride on the lake and visit the hilltop stupa on the other side for nice views. Or hire a car and driver and go up to Sarangkot for some great views of the Annapurnas.
If staying in Kathmandu, consider a taxi to Monkey Temple – Swayambhunath Stupa https://youtu.be/O-udB6Sc_eU?si=YxygXgrfDN0CXr56
Durbar Square is worth a visit. Walk from Kathmandu Guesthouse to Durbar Square – https://youtu.be/9rXmhiTh6Cg?si=WJx_eVPRK8e8ZeUR
If you like trying different food I highly recommend Utse restaurant, my go to place in the city. https://www.utsehotel.com/dinning.html
